options: HNO₂ is a gas at 273 K
HNO₂ is highly explosive when pure
explain: HNO₂ is unstable, so it is prepared in the reaction mixture from NaNO₂ and a mineral acid.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Primary aliphatic amine + HNO₂ liberates which gas, used for estimating –NH₂?
explain: The unstable aliphatic diazonium salt loses N₂ quantitatively (Van Slyke method).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Aromatic diazonium salts are stable at 273–278 K but aliphatic ones are not. Reason?
options: Inductive effect of the alkyl group
explain: The aryl ring delocalises the positive charge on N₂⁺, which stabilises the aromatic diazonium ion.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: N,N-Dimethylaniline + HNO₂ (cold) gives which product?
explain: A tertiary aromatic amine has no N–H, so NO⁺ attacks the activated para position of the ring (green solid).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which species is the electrophile in the nitrosation of amines by HNO₂ in acid?
explain: In acid, HNO₂ forms NO⁺, which attacks the nitrogen of the amine. NO₂⁺ comes from HNO₃/H₂SO₄.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Moles of HCl needed per mole of aniline to form the diazonium chloride with NaNO₂ is?
explain: One HCl forms HNO₂ and one forms the diazonium chloride: ArNH₂ + NaNO₂ + 2HCl → ArN₂Cl + NaCl + 2H₂O.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Benzylamine (C₆H₅CH₂NH₂) + HNO₂ mainly gives which product with N₂?
explain: It is an aliphatic primary amine (–NH₂ on a side-chain carbon), so the diazonium ion is unstable and loses N₂ to give the alcohol.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Why is the sulfonamide from a 1° amine soluble in aqueous KOH?
options: N–H is acidic due to the –SO₂ group
KOH hydrolyses it to the free amine
The N–H is hydrogen bonded to water
It forms a quaternary ammonium salt
explain: The strongly electron-withdrawing SO₂Ph makes the N–H acidic, so KOH forms a soluble potassium salt.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Product of ethylamine with benzenesulfonyl chloride is?
explain: One N–H of the primary amine is replaced: C₆H₅SO₂NHC₂H₅ forms with loss of HCl.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Why does the sulfonamide of a 2° amine not dissolve in alkali?
options: It is a very large molecule
It has no hydrogen on nitrogen
explain: R₂N–SO₂Ph has no N–H, so it cannot form a soluble salt with alkali.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which amine gives no sulfonamide with Hinsberg reagent?
explain: N,N-Dimethylaniline is 3°, with no N–H to substitute.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: The sulfonamide of a 1° amine dissolves in alkali by forming?
options: A soluble potassium salt of sulfonamide
explain: Deprotonation gives [C₆H₅SO₂N⁻R]K⁺, which is water soluble.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Hinsberg test is performed in which medium?
explain: The amine is shaken with benzenesulfonyl chloride in aqueous NaOH or KOH, and the solubility is noted.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which feature of a sulfonamide decides its solubility in alkali?
explain: Only sulfonamides with an acidic N–H (from 1° amines) form soluble salts in alkali.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Direct nitration of aniline with HNO₃/H₂SO₄ gives substantial amount of which isomer?
explain: In strongly acidic medium –NH₂ becomes anilinium –NH₃⁺, a meta director (~47% meta).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Why does direct nitration of aniline give meta product along with para?
options: Steric hindrance blocks ortho and para
explain: HNO₃/H₂SO₄ protonates –NH₂ to –NH₃⁺, which is deactivating and meta-directing.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Why does aniline not undergo Friedel–Crafts reaction?
options: –NH₂ forms salt with AlCl₃, deactivating ring
explain: Lewis base –NH₂ bonds to AlCl₃, giving a positively charged N that strongly deactivates the ring.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Best method to obtain p-nitroaniline as the major product from aniline?
explain: Acetanilide is nitrated mainly at para; hydrolysis then gives p-nitroaniline.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Ethylamine treated with NaNO₂/HCl at 0–5°C mainly gives?
explain: Aliphatic diazonium salts are unstable and decompose at once to alcohol (with other products) and N₂.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which stable benzenediazonium salt can be isolated from solution at room temperature?
explain: Benzenediazonium fluoroborate is water-insoluble and stable at room temperature.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Benzenediazonium chloride in the dry solid state is?
explain: The dry salt decomposes easily and explosively, so it is used in cold aqueous solution.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Excess mineral acid is used in diazotisation mainly to?
explain: Excess acid keeps the amine protonated, so the diazonium ion does not couple with free aniline.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Arenediazonium fluoroborate is stable and isolable mainly because of which anion property?
options: BF₄⁻ is large and poorly nucleophilic
BF₄⁻ forms covalent bond with N
explain: Large, non-nucleophilic BF₄⁻ gives a stable, less water-soluble ionic salt that resists attack on the cation.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Difference between Sandmeyer and Gattermann reactions lies in the:
options: Catalyst: Cu(I) salt vs Cu powder
explain: Sandmeyer uses Cu(I) halide; Gattermann uses Cu powder with HX; yield lower in Gattermann.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which reagent converts ArN₂⁺Cl⁻ to ArBr in Sandmeyer reaction?
explain: Sandmeyer bromination uses Cu₂Br₂/HBr (matching halide).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which reaction cannot be done by direct halogenation, so uses diazonium salt route?
explain: Direct fluorination is too violent and iodination is reversible; diazonium route gives ArF and ArI readily.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Benzenediazonium chloride couples with aniline in weakly acidic medium to give which product?
explain: C₆H₅N₂⁺ attacks para to –NH₂, giving p-aminoazobenzene, a yellow dye.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which pH range is best for coupling of benzenediazonium salt with aniline?
explain: Mild acid keeps free aniline available while diazonium ion stays intact.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which pH range is best for coupling of benzenediazonium salt with phenol?
explain: Mild alkali forms the strongly activating phenoxide without destroying the diazonium ion.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: In azo coupling, the benzenediazonium ion acts as which species?
explain: ArN₂⁺ is a weak electrophile attacking an activated ring (electrophilic substitution).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Why does coupling with aniline fail in strongly acidic medium?
explain: Anilinium ion is deactivated toward electrophilic attack by the diazonium ion.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which compound will NOT undergo azo coupling with benzenediazonium chloride?
explain: Diazonium ion is a weak electrophile; it needs rings activated by –OH or –NR₂/–NH₂.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Azo coupling normally takes place at which position of phenol or aniline?
explain: Para to –OH/–NH₂ is preferred; ortho only if para is blocked.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Benzenediazonium chloride couples with p-cresol at which position?
explain: Para to OH is blocked by CH₃, so coupling occurs ortho to the –OH group.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which functional group is the chromophore characteristic of azo dyes?
explain: The –N=N– group joining two aryl rings gives extended conjugation and colour.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Azo coupling is classified as which type of reaction?
explain: ArN₂⁺ attacks the electron-rich ring of phenol/aniline, replacing H.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Aniline vs toluene (similar molar mass): which has the higher boiling point and why?
explain: Aniline (184 °C) has intermolecular N–H···N H-bonding; toluene (111 °C) lacks it.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Inorganic products formed along with RNC in the carbylamine reaction are?
explain: Three HCl are lost from the amine and CHCl₃, and KOH neutralises them to give 3KCl + 3H₂O.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Alkyl isocyanides are resistant to hydrolysis by which reagent?
explain: Isocyanides are stable to alkali and are hydrolysed only by acids, which is why the test works in KOH.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: After the Hinsberg test, the alkali-insoluble residue from a 3° amine dissolves on adding?
explain: A 3° amine is unreacted and basic, so dilute HCl converts it to a soluble ammonium salt.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Aniline with benzenesulfonyl chloride in the Hinsberg test gives which compound?
explain: The 1° aryl amine gives ArNH–SO₂Ph, which retains an acidic N–H and so dissolves in KOH.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: The alkali-insoluble sulfonamide of a 2° amine, when treated with dilute HCl, will?
explain: The N,N-disubstituted sulfonamide is neutral and non-basic, so it stays insoluble in both alkali and acid.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Sandmeyer replacement of ArN₂⁺ by Cl using Cu(I) proceeds mainly through which type of mechanism?
explain: Cu(I) transfers an electron to ArN₂⁺, giving an aryl radical, which abstracts Cl from Cu(II)Cl.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: On warming ArN₂⁺Cl⁻ with ethanol, ArH forms along with which by-product from ethanol?
formula: ArN₂⁺Cl⁻ + CH₃CH₂OH → ArH + CH₃CHO + N₂ + HCl
explain: Ethanol acts as a reducing agent and is oxidised to ethanal while the diazonium group is replaced by H.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Among isomeric butylamines, which has the lowest boiling point because of its compact branched shape?
explain: Branching reduces surface area and van der Waals forces: tert-butyl ≈ 45 °C, n-butyl ≈ 78 °C.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Dichlorocarbene from CHCl₃ + KOH is generated through which type of step?
explain: OH⁻ removes H from CHCl₃; CCl₃⁻ then loses Cl⁻ from the same carbon, so it is α-elimination.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: In Hinsberg test, a 3° amine in aqueous KOH leaves the reagent C₆H₅SO₂Cl mainly as?
explain: 3° amine has no N–H, so no stable sulfonamide forms; alkali hydrolyses the sulfonyl chloride to the sulfonate salt.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: A tertiary amine boils higher than an alkane of similar molar mass mainly due to?
options: Larger van der Waals surface area
Dipole–dipole attraction from polar C–N bonds
explain: 3° amines lack N–H, but the polar C–N bonds and lone pair give dipole–dipole forces, so bp > alkane.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Acylation of an amine by RCOCl proceeds through which type of mechanism?
explain: The amine N attacks C=O (addition), then Cl⁻ leaves (elimination): nucleophilic acyl substitution via a tetrahedral intermediate.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: In the carbylamine reaction, the carbon of the –NC group in the product is supplied by which reagent?
options: The alkyl group R of the amine
explain: CHCl₃ gives :CCl₂, whose carbon becomes the isocyanide carbon; the amine supplies only N.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Chief reason arenediazonium salts are such versatile synthetic intermediates?
options: Cl⁻ is easily oxidised by the ring
The N–N single bond is very strong
N₂ is an excellent leaving group
explain: –N₂⁺ is replaced by many groups because N₂ leaves very easily; –N₂⁺ is also electron-withdrawing, not activating.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: In ArNH₂ + NaNO₂ + 2HCl → ArN₂⁺Cl⁻ + X, X is?
explain: Balancing H and O gives NaCl and two H₂O.
